solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bombshell hasn't the head for drink

indicators.note: lacking its head means the synonym loses its first letter here

parts.note: a bombshell is a shock, a sudden surprise

explanation.surface: A glamorous film star is too dizzy to handle her drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't the head' drops the S from SHOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is a German white wine, the British name for Rhine wine.

clue.text: Sight defect produced by excessive work starts to impair academic

parts.note: hyper- is the prefix meaning excessive or over
OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words supply their first letters only

explanation.surface: An eye problem arising from overwork begins to hamper a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes I and A from 'impair academic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperopia is long-sightedness, a refractive error of the eye.

clue.text: Prepare to swindle officer cadet on vacation

parts.note: to con is to swindle
CO is a commanding officer

indicators.note: vacated, the word is emptied of its inside, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A con artist plans to cheat a young officer trainee while he is on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties 'cadet' to CT.
explanation.definitionFit: To concoct is to prepare a dish or plan by mixing ingredients together.

clue.text: It's forbidden to strike rebounding balls

indicators.note: bouncing back signals that the word for strike is written backwards

parts.note: to bat is to strike a ball
O is a ball shape, and two of them make balls

explanation.surface: A sports rule bans hitting balls that bounce back off a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebounding' turns BAT into TAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is something prohibited by custom, so the clue's phrase describes it.

clue.text: Man interrupting singer after Tosca's entrance gets tongue-lashing

indicators.note: after puts the singer's piece behind the opening letter
a word's entrance is its first letter, here of the opera's name
breaking into means one word goes inside another

parts.note: an alto is a singer
a man in chess is a piece, here the king

explanation.surface: At an opera, a man barges into a singer's entrance in Tosca and is scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece, here the king. 'interrupting' signals the insertion and 'after' puts the result behind Tosca's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a scolding, the same as a tongue-lashing.

clue.text: Scrooge's take on weather in Islamic state?

parts.note: Scrooge in Dickens's A Christmas Carol scoffs 'Bah! Humbug!'
rain is a kind of weather

explanation.surface: How would Scrooge grumble about the climate of a Muslim country?
explanation.walkthrough: BAH is Scrooge's famous dismissive exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bahrain is a Gulf kingdom whose state religion is Islam; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Plants depicted by fine artists

parts.note: OK means fine
RAs are Royal Academicians, artists

explanation.surface: Painters have made some nice pictures of vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a flowering plant grown for its edible pods, also called lady's fingers.

clue.text: Fascination with drug to lose lustre

parts.note: a fad is a short-lived craze or fascination
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: An obsession with narcotics makes someone lose their sparkle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fade is to become dull, losing brightness or shine.

clue.text: This sort of channel could create a riot

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: set the letters TO AIR free, i.e. rearrange them, and they make these two words

explanation.surface: A provocative TV channel might stir up a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer splits as 'free' (an anagram signal) and TO AIR, and freeing TO AIR creates A RIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Free-to-air television channels broadcast without any subscription charge.

clue.text: Players must support director that's to shape The Crucible's lead

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting puts this piece beneath the others

parts.note: i.e. (id est) means that is
the cast are the players in a show

explanation.surface: A theatre's actors back their director in staging Arthur Miller's play The Crucible.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crucible looks like Miller's play, but read as a melting pot its lead is the metal: die-casting shapes molten lead in a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: To die-cast is to form metal objects by forcing molten metal into a mould.

clue.text: I make a point by removing dead wood

definitions.text: I make a point by removing dead wood

parts.words: I make a point by removing dead wood
parts.note: sounds like a manager clearing out staff, but literally a device that shaves wood to sharpen a writing tool

explanation.surface: A ruthless boss boasts of proving a point by sacking deadwood.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'dead wood' is the timber casing of a pencil, shaved away to form its tip.
explanation.definitionFit: This gadget cuts away the wooden casing of a pencil to give it a sharp point.

clue.text: Plane figures in Spooner's order to attack East Sussex town

indicators.note: Spooner's version means the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: BOMB! is an order to attack
Rye is a town in East Sussex, England

explanation.surface: A military command to bombard a small English seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: BOMB RYE with its first sounds swapped is 'romb bye', said like the answer. Rye is a historic small town in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhombi are rhombuses, four-sided flat shapes with equal sides.

clue.text: Dog Day Afternoon impresses one: note Pacino's in the lead

indicators.note: being in the lead puts this name at the front of the answer

parts.note: Al Pacino, the actor, gives his first name

indicators.note: to impress here is to press into, so the following one goes inside

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday
A is short for afternoon, as in a.m./p.m. timetables
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Dog Day Afternoon, a film starring Al Pacino, leaves an impression on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog Day Afternoon' is a 1975 Pacino film; 'Dog' splits off as the definition. 'impresses' puts I inside SATA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alsatian is a breed of dog, known in America as the German shepherd.

clue.text: Something nasty by way of incomplete knowledge

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: incomplete means the little word is cut short to its first letter

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or knowledge

explanation.surface: Little learning is dangerous: a half-knowledge produces something unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' shortens 'of' to O. 'Gen' is British slang for the lowdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathogen is a germ, virus or other agent causing disease, plainly unpleasant.

clue.text: Eminent judge goes into decline after losing face for rowdy behaviour

indicators.note: going into puts the judge inside the other letters

parts.note: high means eminent or lofty

indicators.note: losing its face means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: sinks means declines

explanation.surface: A senior judge's career is in decline after a humiliation over disorderly conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' is a verb here (sinks), and 'after losing face' drops its first letter; 'goes into' sets the judge between the two other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: High jinks is boisterous fun or rowdy carrying-on.

clue.text: Features of Barnet clearly detailed by Eliot's precursors?

indicators.note: de-tailed means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: plain is clearly, as in plain to see
the initials before the poet T. S. Eliot's surname

explanation.surface: Details of Barnet, north London, were set out clearly by the poet's forerunners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barnet' is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), not the London borough. 'detailed' cuts PLAIN to PLAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaits are braids, which are styles worn in the hair.

clue.text: Leading theatre school not right to withdraw course for West Indians

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: top means leading or foremost
rep is repertory theatre

indicators.note: without right means the R is dropped

parts.note: a prep is a preparatory school

explanation.surface: A top drama school, unable to cope, pulls a course designed for Caribbean students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' cuts PREP to PEP; 'to withdraw' turns TOPREPPEP back to front. 'Course' is a dish, not a study programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperpot is a spicy meat stew that is a national dish in the Caribbean, notably Guyana.

clue.text: Doubtful about wearing infected animal's skin

indicators.note: the infected word wears, i.e. surrounds, the short word for about

parts.note: septic means infected
C is circa, about

indicators.note: an animal's skin is its outside, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure about putting on the hide of a diseased creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is C for circa, which 'wearing' places inside; 'skin' keeps only the outside letters of 'animal's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sceptical means inclined to doubt or question.

clue.text: Slow NY lawyer put in charge of exchange

indicators.note: putting one piece in means it goes inside the other

parts.note: agio is the fee charged for changing currency
a DA is a district attorney, as in New York

explanation.surface: A sluggish New York lawyer is given responsibility for a stock exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge of exchange' is not 'in charge': agio is a banking term for the premium paid on currency exchange; 'put in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction for a slow tempo.

clue.text: Trickled through dehydrated casing very softly

indicators.note: casing means the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: dried means dehydrated
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very softly

explanation.surface: Liquid seeped quietly through a dried-out shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very softly' is the musical marking pianissimo, which 'casing' wraps inside the dried word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dripped means fell in drops, so trickled slowly.

clue.text: Witty comments about terms at St Andrews?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
par and tee are golf terms; St Andrews in Scotland is the home of golf

explanation.surface: Banter about the language used on a famous Scottish golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: St Andrews is the Scottish town known as the home of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, witty conversation full of clever replies.

clue.text: Not completely? For Americans, though, being ahead would make it so

definitions.text: Not completely? For Americans, though, being ahead would make it so

parts.words: Not completely? For Americans, though, being ahead would make it so
parts.note: the American spelling of though is tho; put it ahead of the answer and you have a word meaning completely

explanation.surface: A puzzle about partial completeness and American usage.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans spell 'though' as THO; placed ahead of the answer it makes THOROUGHLY, completely, so the answer means not completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughly means approximately, so not exactly or completely.

clue.text: Advertised piece of cobalt rail edging

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A blue-metal edging strip for a railing was promoted in an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail a programme or film is to advertise it in advance with a trailer.

clue.text: Entirely pointlessly in June, unfortunately, I just abandoned physical activity

indicators.note: unfortunately signals the letters fall into a different, unlucky order
entirely without points means every compass point letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone gave up their exercise routine in June for no reason at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entirely pointlessly' removes all compass points (N, N, E) from IN JUNE, leaving IJU; 'unfortunately' rearranges IJU with IJUST. 'abandoned' is only surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Jiu-jitsu is a Japanese martial art, a form of physical combat training.

clue.text: Swimmer needs time to cover most of course

indicators.note: in a down entry, covering puts this letter on top
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a route is a course

explanation.surface: A swimmer needs time to get through most of the race course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts ROUTE to ROUT; 'to cover' sets T above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater fish, and fish are swimmers.

clue.text: Wandering bombastic speech by former church leader

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen, who was Supreme Governor of the Church of England
a rant is a bombastic speech

explanation.surface: A retired bishop rambles through a pompous sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Queen Elizabeth II; the British monarch heads the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means straying or travelling about, as a knight-errant wandered.

clue.text: Inept couple both misinterpreted welcoming notice on door?

indicators.note: misinterpreted means the letters are read in the wrong way, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A hapless couple both misread a sign on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign reading OPEN TO THE PUBLIC on a door invites everyone inside.

clue.text: Fancies spending a day in Rome

indicators.note: spending a means losing that letter, as money is spent

parts.note: ideas are fancies, notions

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of passing a day in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spending' removes the A from IDEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The ides was a fixed date in the ancient Roman calendar, the 15th or 13th.

clue.text: Go to special sweetheart at last?

definitions.text: Go to special sweetheart at last?

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
S stands for special, as in the S-level (Special paper) exam

indicators.note: at last means only the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Finally going off to meet that one special lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes T from 'sweetheart'. Read whole, the clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret meeting between lovers, which this outing is.

clue.text: Image brides hold in their hearts?

indicators.note: the hearts of these words are their central letters, two from each

explanation.surface: A picture that brides cherish deep in their hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in their hearts' takes ID from 'brides' and OL from 'hold'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image or statue worshipped as a god.
